title: Advanced For Loops
intro: Iteration Structures: Working with For Loops
bullets: End a for loop with break.

title: Nesting for Loops
paragraphs: A for loop can be placed inside another for loop.
The inner loop completes all iterations at the current outer value. The outer loop then advances.
Here, each row visits columns 0 and 1. The inner loop restarts when the row changes.

title: Reading Positions with enumerate
paragraphs: enumerate provides a position and an item during each iteration.
The variable index receives the position. The variable name receives the item.
The default starting position is 0.

title: Choosing Where the Count Starts
paragraphs: The start argument changes the first count from enumerate.
Here, start=1 numbers the items from 1.
This changes the count shown by enumerate. It does not change the positions in the original list.

title: Pairing Items with zip
paragraphs: zip takes one item from each iterable during an iteration.
Here, each name is paired with the grade at the same position.
zip stops when the shortest iterable runs out of items.
code:
names = ["Alex", "Sam"]
grades = [82, 91]

for name, grade in zip(names, grades):
    print(name, grade)

title: Ending a for Loop with break
paragraphs: break ends the loop immediately.
Here, the loop stops when number reaches 3. That value is not displayed.
Python continues with the first instruction after the loop.

title: Stopping a Search
paragraphs: A search can stop when its target is found.
Here, break runs after Charlie is found. The loop does not visit David.
The final message is outside the loop. It is displayed after the search ends.

title: Skipping an Iteration with continue
paragraphs: continue skips the remaining instructions in the current iteration.
The for loop then takes its next value.
Here, number is not displayed when it is 2. The values 3 and 4 are still displayed.

title: break Inside Nested Loops
paragraphs: A break inside the inner loop ends only that loop.
The outer loop continues with its next value.
Here, each row displays only column 0. The inner loop ends when column reaches 1.

title: Wrap Up
bullets: A nested loop completes its inner iterations for each outer value.
Use enumerate to receive a position and an item.
Use zip to visit related items together. It stops at the shortest iterable.
Use break to end the nearest containing loop.
Use continue to skip the rest of the current iteration.
